rows.gate: The retrieved evidence counts female agricultural HOLDERS (the person making the major management decisions on the holding), not female LANDOWNERS. This is exactly the open definitional question flagged for this row: the indicator name says women who OWN land, while the available canonical statistic counts operators, who may rent rather than own. rows.gate: The indicator name "Digital land/plot registration" is satisfied only partly by the best available Egyptian evidence, which sits on the economy-wide side of the unratified definition. The National Real Estate ID system is a property IDENTIFICATION database covering all real estate — "freestanding house, apartment, factory, office, or vacant plot" (Al-Ahram, T5) — not a register of legal title, and not an agricultural usufruct/holding register. It does explicitly extend to farmland: the Minister of Agriculture "emphasized the importance of linking the national real estate ID to each housing unit—whether owned, rented, or inherited—as well as to agricultural land". The separate legal-title track is the World Bank-financed Modernization of Egyptian Property Registration Project (P177720, US$230m, Ministry of Justice), whose objective is "to establish the foundations of a modern and efficient land administration and management system at national level and scale up property registration in selected new urban communities" — i.e. urban new communities, not agricultural plots. Agricultural holding records themselves remain paper-based in the source evidence: the 2009-2010 Agricultural Census used "Paper-based forms ... for both phases of the census fieldwork". No published figure isolates digitally registered AGRICULTURAL plots or holdings.
